newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Bank of Korea steps in, sells dlr to support won.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Korea steps in, sells dlr to support won.

text.p: The Bank of Korea intervened in the interbank market in Tuesday morning trading, selling dollars to support the won, dealers said.
They said the bank began selling dollars as the won fell to a new 83-month low of 857.00 to the U.S. unit.
Dealers said the won fell rapidly after opening at 856.40 on import-related dollar demand and the yen's weakness against the dollar on world markets.
Speculation that a large trade deficit would continue to weigh on the won also helped push the won lower, they added.
The 857 won/dollar rate was the local currency's lowest level since the nation introduced a market-average system in March 1990.
